title: The board /rankings renders is not the board GET /api/data serves: the stock frontend body {"tep_multiplier":1.15} changes 627 of 740 ranks and 654 tiers while the response stamps isCustomized:false
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Custom source configurations flow through the SAME canonical pipeline as the default board'; the delta is described as 'only the override-sensitive fields' merged onto the cached base, and rankingsOverride.isCustomized reports whether the board was customised.
observed: A live browser load of http://127.0.0.1:3000/rankings POSTs {"tep_multiplier":1.15} (the /settings default) to /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta. That response is a materially different board from GET /api/data: 627 of 740 canonicalConsensusRank values differ, 654 canonicalTierId values differ, 135 rankDerivedValue values differ (82 TE, 50 PICK, 3 other) — yet rankingsOverride.isCustomized is false and no field on the response says the board diverged. Cause: an explicit tep_multiplier bypasses the measured base->tepp TE basis curve (ADR-015, 1.209 at the top rising toward 2.05 down the board) and substitutes a flat 1.15 — the exact constant ADR-015 removed for sitting below the entire observed range. Deep TEs lose up to 21% of value and ~200 ranks. The server-side engines (trade suggestions, finder, angles, terminal, simulate) all read latest_contract_data, i.e. the GET /api/data board — so the page and the advice disagree by construction.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/rankings/overrides?view=delta' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tep_multiplier":1.15}' -o /tmp/tep.json; .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W03/delta_rt.py  # and see tep-board-divergence.json
reproduction.expected: delta ranks/tiers/values identical to GET /api/data when isCustomized is false, or isCustomized:true plus a stated reason
reproduction.actual: 627 rank / 654 tier / 135 value divergences with isCustomized:false

numericProof.formula: pageValue = blended_TE_value_on_base_basis * flat_tep_multiplier  (explicit slider bypasses convert_te_value base->tepp)

userImpact: A manager reads Tyler Conklin at #666 / 1,142 on /rankings, then opens /trade where the engine values him at 1,450 (#469) — a 21% price difference on the same asset, in the same session, with no label distinguishing the two boards. Every TE trade priced from the rankings page is priced off a board no engine uses.

priorFinding.note: A12-F05 identified that a TEP-only body reaches the pipeline as source_overrides=={} (which is how it clears the 'not source_overrides' guard); it framed the consequence as a snapshot write. The board divergence itself and the isCustomized:false mislabel are new.

whatWorks: The delta payload is internally consistent with its own view=full sibling — zero field mismatches across all 1,092 rows and all 43 _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS (W03-F002).
rootCause: normalize_tep_multiplier extracts tep_multiplier as a reserved top-level knob that normalize_source_overrides deliberately skips, so the body produces source_overrides == {} and rankingsOverride.isCustomized == False, while tep_multiplier is still threaded into build_rankings_delta_payload and does change the board. 'Customised' is defined as 'has source overrides' rather than 'differs from the canonical board'.
requiredRepair: Either (a) build the canonical GET /api/data contract with the same default tep_multiplier the frontend posts so the two boards are one board, or (b) stamp isCustomized:true (or a distinct boardVariant/tepMultiplier field) on any response whose tep_multiplier differs from the contract's, and thread the same multiplier into the engine paths. Separately, decide whether the /settings default should be the flat 1.15 that ADR-015 retired.
dependencies: Interacts with the value-pipeline workstream (ADR-015 TE basis) and the trade-engine workstream (engine board selection).

title: For one and the same request the delta view round-trips every _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS field exactly — 0 mismatches over 1,092 rows x 43 fields, verified with and without a real source override
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'every field in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS round-trips through a manual merge identically to the full-contract path'.
observed: Verified three ways on the live stack. (1) Empty override body: GET /api/data vs POST ?view=full — 0 mismatches on all 43 delta fields across 1,092 rows. (2) Same body, view=delta vs view=full — 0 presence mismatches, 0 value mismatches. (3) Real override disabling ktcSfTep + dlfSf + fantasyCalc — delta vs full still 0 mismatches. Key sets are identical (1,092 == 1,092). The delta is 3.92 MB vs 11.79 MB full (67% smaller), matching the documented ~70%.
userImpact: None — this is a clean bill of health for the delta shape itself.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding disputed the delta round-trip for the fields it carries; the prior findings are about fields it omits (see W03-F003).

whatWorks: The delta field list, the merge key (displayName), and activePlayerIds all behave as documented.

title: Seven fields change under a source override but are absent from _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS; sourceAudit (515 rows) and rankChange (602 rows) reach the UI carrying the default board's answer beside override values
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: view=delta 'returns only the override-sensitive fields per player'.
observed: Diffing GET /api/data against POST ?view=full with {ktcSfTep:off, dlfSf:off, fantasyCalc:off}, seven fields change that are NOT in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS: offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue (606 rows), rankChange (602), sourceAudit (515), _blendedValueUncapped (510), pickRookieAnchor (57), singleSourceValuePenaltyApplied (1), twoWayPlayerBoost (1). mergeRankingsDelta copies only the delta entry's own keys onto the cached base row, so all seven keep the default board's values. sourceAudit drives the single-source tooltip (rankings-helpers.js:131 reads row.sourceAudit.reason) and its expectedSources/unmatchedSources are computed without consulting the overrides at all, so a source the user switched OFF is reported as a coverage failure. rankChange drives the movement arrow in the '#' column, the risers/fallers panel and signal-engine's 'rank rising N on the last scrape' text.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W03/delta_rt.py  # section 'FIELDS THAT CHANGE UNDER OVERRIDE BUT ARE NOT IN _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS'

numericProof.formula: count(rows where base[field] != overrideFull[field] and field not in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS)

userImpact: With custom source weights, a player's movement arrow and Source Audit panel describe the board the user turned off. On view=full (a public API surface) the arrow is worse than stale: it is default-rank minus override-rank, rendered with the aria-label 'moved up N since the previous scrape' when nothing scraped.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed at runtime on the live stack. A12-F06 measured 571 rankChange rows on a different override set; I measure 602 on {ktcSfTep,dlfSf,fantasyCalc} off. PRIOR-A12-F07 (sourceAudit, 510 rows) also confirmed — I measure 515, and confirm expectedSources ignores the override.

whatWorks: Every field that IS in the list round-trips exactly (W03-F002).
rootCause: _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS was curated by hand and has drifted from the set of fields _compute_unified_rankings actually recomputes; nothing tests the complement.
requiredRepair: Add the four user-visible ones (rankChange, sourceAudit, pickRookieAnchor, offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue) to _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS, and add a test that diffs a default build against an override build and fails on any changed field outside the list. Separately, make _expected_sources_for_position consult source_overrides so a disabled source is not reported as an unmatched one.

title: confidenceBucket rises when sources disappear: dropping one real source raises the published label on 237 of 679 rows (34.9%), and 'high' is more common at 3 sources (11.1%) than at 4 (2.3%)
claimUnderTest: The contract publishes confidenceBuckets.high = '2+ sources, sourceRankPercentileSpread <= 0.08' and the /rankings column tooltip says 'High / Medium / Low confidence based on how many sources matched and how tightly they agree.'
observed: Source count enters the rule only as the gate source_count >= 2; beyond that the label is a pure function of the percentile spread, which is computed ONLY over sources that ranked the player. Removing a source therefore cannot widen the statistic and usually narrows it. Replaying the live board through the production functions _percentile_rank_spread + _compute_confidence_bucket and deleting exactly one real source per row: 237 of 679 rows (34.9%) get a STRICTLY HIGHER label. The board-wide distribution is non-monotone and largely inverted: n=3 -> 11.1% high, n=4 -> 2.3%, n=12 -> 45.8%, n=15 -> 0%. The 5-source trim boundary (_PERCENTILE_SPREAD_TRIM_MIN_N) adds a step discontinuity: 2.3% high at n=4 vs 26.5% at n=5. Two rows both badged 'High' therefore do not mean the same thing, and the tooltip's 'how many sources matched' is not in the formula.

reproduction.expected: 0 rows improve when evidence is removed; monotone non-decreasing high-rate vs source count

inputs.scope: ranked non-pick rows with >=3 effective sources
inputs.example: Akheem Mesidor: 4 sources, percentileSpread 0.2378 -> 'low'; drop idpShow -> 'high'

numericProof.formula: bucket = high if n>=2 and pctSpread<=0.08 else medium if n>=2 and pctSpread<=0.20 else low; pctSpread = max-min (trimmed at n>=5) of rawRank/poolSize over PRESENT sources only

userImpact: A manager filters /rankings to 'High confidence' to find safe trade targets and gets rows that are high precisely because 12 of 14 boards never rated the player. Confidence is being read as evidence strength; it measures only the agreement of whoever showed up.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed and quantified board-wide: A12-F03 gave named single examples (CJ Donaldson etc.); I measure the rate at 34.9% by replaying the production functions with one source deleted, and add the n=4 vs n=5 trim discontinuity.

whatWorks: Every stamped confidenceBucket on the live board reproduces exactly from its own inputs — 0 mismatches over 709 ranked non-pick rows. The rule is implemented as published; the rule itself is the defect.
rootCause: Coverage and agreement are collapsed into one label whose only coverage term is a binary n>=2 gate, and the agreement statistic is computed over present sources only. softFallbackCount / sourceAudit.reason (which do know about absent coverage) are never consulted.
requiredRepair: Make coverage a first-class term — e.g. cap the bucket at 'medium' when matchedSources/expectedSources is below a threshold, or publish coverage as a second badge. At minimum, stop claiming 'how many sources matched' in the tooltip while the formula ignores it.

title: confidenceBucket is agreement about RANK ORDER, not about the value it is rendered beside: 21 of 89 'high' rows have per-source value dispersion above 30% of the published value (worst 76%)
claimUnderTest: The Confidence badge sits in the same table row as the VALUE column and is read as 'how sure are we about this number'.
observed: The bucket's input is sourceRankPercentileSpread (rawRank/poolSize space). The number the badge sits beside is rankDerivedValue, blended from sourceRankMeta[k].valueContribution. The row already carries the value-space statistic — hillValueSpread, the stdev of those contributions — and it is never consulted. On the live board, of 89 ranked non-pick rows badged 'high', 21 (23.6%) have hillValueSpread/rankDerivedValue > 0.30. Worst: Jadon Canady, value 871, hillValueSpread 665.4 = 76% relative dispersion, badged High on 2 sources. Medians do separate correctly by bucket (high 0.072 / medium 0.130 / low 0.196), so the signal is directionally real — the tail is what is mislabelled.

reproduction.actual: 21/89 high rows exceed 30% relative value dispersion

userImpact: A user sizing a trade around a 'High confidence' 871 is looking at sources that priced the player anywhere from ~200 to ~1,540. The badge suppresses exactly the uncertainty a trade needs.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed; my denominator differs (89 high rows on this build vs 107 on theirs) so the rate is 23.6% vs 18.7%, same defect.

whatWorks: hillValueSpread is stamped on 895 rows and is a correct stdev of the value contributions — the value-space statistic already exists.
rootCause: The bucket was migrated from ordinal spread to percentile spread to fix a depth-comparability problem, but neither version was ever in value space, and the row's own value-space statistic post-dates the rule.
requiredRepair: Add a value-space guard: demote to 'medium' (or publish a second axis) when hillValueSpread/rankDerivedValue exceeds a stated threshold. Pin the threshold in tests.

title: marketGapDirection averages ordinal ranks across source pools of 169-903 rows; 55.4% of offense rows and 95.8% of pick rows carry the OPPOSITE label under pool normalization, and Calvin Ridley renders BUY on /rankings because of it
claimUnderTest: marketGapDirection/Magnitude 'quantify the disagreement between retail and expert consensus' and drive the /rankings EDGE column plus the trade page's BUY/SELL signal.
observed: _compute_market_gap takes the arithmetic mean of retail ranks and of consensus ranks and subtracts them — raw ordinals, no pool normalization. The same module's _percentile_rank_spread docstring states this is invalid: 'an effective spread of 100 doesn't mean the sources disagree, it means one is on a 1-185 scale and the other is on a 1-600 scale.' Live pool sizes: dlfIdp 169, dlfSf 278, ktcSfTep 499, idpTradeCalc 903. Recomputing the same comparison in percentile space (rawRank/poolSize, exactly what the sibling function uses) flips the direction on 214 of 386 offense rows (55.4%) and 23 of 24 pick rows (95.8%). Confirmed in the live DOM: Calvin Ridley renders EDGE = BUY on http://127.0.0.1:3000/rankings. Separately, all 293 ranked IDP rows carry direction 'none' because KTC publishes no defenders, so the EDGE column is permanently blank for 40% of the board (honestly, but the column has no coverage note). frontend/lib/display-helpers.js::marketEdge recomputes the identical ordinal-mean logic client-side, so the frontend mirrors rather than checks the backend.

numericProof.formula: ordinal: diff = consensusMean - retailMean = 269.769 - 325 = -55.23 -> consensus_premium (BUY). percentile: 0.6616 - 0.6513 = +0.0103 -> retail_premium (the opposite).

userImpact: A manager opens /rankings, sees Calvin Ridley flagged BUY ("experts value him above retail — buy low from a retail-first partner"), and offers for a player the retail market actually prices ABOVE the expert consensus. The same field drives getPlayerEdge on /trade, the buy/sell advanced filter and the EdgeRail. No caveat is shown.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed independently on the live stack with a new worked example (Calvin Ridley) and live DOM proof of the rendered BUY badge. My rates: offense 55.4% (prior 47%), picks 95.8% (prior 97%).

whatWorks: marketGapDirection/Magnitude reproduce exactly from effectiveSourceRanks — 0 mismatches over 740 ranked rows. The arithmetic is right; the inputs are incommensurable.
rootCause: _compute_market_gap predates the percentile-normalisation work that fixed the same class of bug in _percentile_rank_spread, and was never revisited when the source registry grew from 3 similar-depth boards to 21 boards spanning 169-903 rows.
requiredRepair: Normalise both sides by each source's own pool size before differencing (reuse the pool-size map _percentile_rank_spread already builds), re-express marketGapMagnitude in percentile points, and re-derive MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF / MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP for the new units. Update frontend/lib/display-helpers.js::marketEdge in lockstep or delete it in favour of the backend stamp.
dependencies: Blocks any re-tuning of MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF; touches the same effectiveSourceRanks map as W03-F004.

title: 127 tiers on a 740-row board, and 100% of the 122 detected boundaries are a smaller value drop than the adjacent rows' own source disagreement (93.4% are inside the standard error)
claimUnderTest: src/api/data_contract.py:2137-2140: 'Tiers land where the per-player value gap is unusually large relative to the local rolling-median gap: a 400-point drop from rank 12->13 is a boundary; a 3-point drop from 312->313 is not.'
observed: detect_tiers normalises each gap by a local rolling median and breaks at score >= 2.0, which is scale-free — so boundaries fire at the same RATE at every depth regardless of how small the absolute drop is. Live: 127 tiers over 740 ranked rows, min tier size 3, max 14. Boundary raw gaps: min 1.0, median 8.0, max 370.0 on a 0-9999 scale. Eight boundaries are a 1-point drop (e.g. Upton Stout -> DeShon Elliott, gap 1.0, score 3.00) — a case the docstring says explicitly must not be a boundary. Cross-checked against the rows' own uncertainty: 122 of 122 boundaries have a gap smaller than max(sourceSpread) of the two adjacent rows (median sourceSpread on the board is 223.6), and 114 of 122 (93.4%) are smaller than max(hillValueSpread/sqrt(n)), the standard error of the blend. Tiers reproduce deterministically (0 mismatches re-running detect_tiers on the payload), so this is a methodology defect, not a bug.

reproduction.expected: boundaries at genuine value cliffs, i.e. gaps large relative to measurement noise
reproduction.actual: 127 tiers; median boundary gap 8.0 vs median sourceSpread 223.6; 122/122 boundaries inside adjacent-row spread; 114/122 inside SEM

numericProof.formula: isMeaningful = rawGap > max(hillValueSpread/sqrt(n)) for the two adjacent rows

userImpact: A manager treats 'Tier 63' and 'Tier 64' as a real quality break and refuses a trade across it, when the two players are separated by less than the noise in their own valuations. Tier is also a filter facet on /rankings (tier: exact match), so users can slice the board on a distinction that does not exist.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed exactly (127 tiers, median boundary 8.0). New: the comparison against the rows' own sourceSpread and standard error — 122/122 and 114/122 respectively — which shows the boundaries are inside measurement noise, not merely small.

whatWorks: compact_ranks_and_tiers is genuinely the one ranker: ranks are contiguous 1..740, value is monotone non-increasing along rank with 0 inversions, and re-running detect_tiers on the served values reproduces every canonicalTierId exactly.
rootCause: A scale-free gap detector with a fixed score threshold and no absolute-magnitude floor, applied to a series whose per-point uncertainty is roughly 30x the median detected gap.
requiredRepair: Add an absolute floor (or an uncertainty-relative floor using the hillValueSpread already on each row) to detect_tiers before a break is accepted, and cap the tier count to something a user can reason about. Pin both in tests.

title: marketConfidence is structurally confined to [0.20, 0.594] because its site-count term divides by 8 while the scraper only ever sees 3 sources; 376 of 840 rows carry the identical value 0.48
claimUnderTest: marketConfidence is stamped on the contract as a 0-1 confidence number and materialized onto every board row as row.confidence.
observed: conf = clamp(0.65*clamp(siteCount/8, 0.20, 1.00) + 0.35*clamp(1 - min(cv,0.35)/0.35, 0.20, 1.00), 0.20, 1.00). siteCount counts only the scraper's own numeric dash keys — ktc, ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc — so siteCount <= 3, siteScore <= 0.375, and conf <= 0.375*0.65 + 1.0*0.35 = 0.59375. Measured on the live payload: 840 rows, min 0.3457, max 0.5938 (equals the theoretical cap to four decimals), and 376 rows at exactly 0.48 — the value produced by siteCount=1 with perfect agreement. The other 12-18 sources that actually drive rankDerivedValue arrive via CSV enrichment AFTER the scraper's composite and are invisible to this statistic; a row with sourceCount 14 and a row with sourceCount 1 can both read 0.48. It is also listed in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS as if a source override could move it, which it cannot.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys,collections; d=json.load(sys.stdin); mc=[r['marketConfidence'] for r in d['playersArray'] if r.get('marketConfidence') is not None]; print(len(mc), min(mc), max(mc), collections.Counter(mc).most_common(3))"
reproduction.expected: a 0-1 statistic that uses the full range

userImpact: Any surface that thresholds this field treats the whole board as mid-confidence. The one consumer that did (terminal's low_conf_unstable at <0.35) was retired for exactly this reason, so today the field is shipped on 840 rows and read for nothing — dead weight in the payload with a misleading name.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed to four decimals on this build (max 0.5938 == theoretical cap). PRIOR-A12-F16 also confirmed: 376 rows at 0.48 (prior said 375), and the field is indeed in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS.

whatWorks: The formula reproduces exactly from the scraper inputs; nothing is miscomputed.
rootCause: A /8.0 divisor sized for a ~10-scraper-source era, never updated when source ingestion moved to post-scrape CSV enrichment.
requiredRepair: Either recompute it from the contract's real sourceCount after enrichment, or delete the field and the row.confidence materializer. Keeping a 0-1-shaped field that cannot exceed 0.594 is worse than not shipping it.

title: identityConfidence is a four-valued proxy for 'does this row have a Sleeper ID' presented as a 0-1 score; 937 of 1,092 rows score 1.00 without any name, position or source evidence being checked, and the 0.85 branch never fires
claimUnderTest: Docstring: 'Score how confident we are that this row represents the right entity. 1.00 — has a non-empty playerId'.
observed: has_id short-circuits before every other check, so a row with a Sleeper ID and a flat position/source contradiction still scores 1.00. Live distribution over 1,092 rows: 1.00 x937 (exactly the 937 rows with a non-empty playerId), 0.95 x144 (picks, via the asset_class=='pick' short-circuit), 0.70 x11. The 0.85 'partial_evidence' branch fires zero times. Reproduced exactly with the production function — 0 mismatches — so the number is faithfully computed; it just measures ID presence rather than match correctness, while the join that attaches 19 of 21 sources' votes runs on a normalized NAME key.

reproduction.expected: a graded score reflecting match evidence
reproduction.actual: {1.0: 937, 0.95: 144, 0.7: 11}; rows with a playerId = 937; 0.85 branch count = 0

numericProof.expected: different if any evidence beyond ID presence is used

userImpact: Low today — no user-facing surface renders it. It is a trap for the next consumer: a filter on 'identityConfidence >= 0.95' would admit every mis-joined row that happens to carry an ID.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed exactly (937/144/11, 0.85 dead). PRIOR-A24-F02 also confirmed: 937/1092 = 85.8% at 1.00 on ID presence alone.

whatWorks: The function is deterministic and reproduces from the row verbatim; identityMethod honestly names the branch ('canonical_id'), so the provenance is at least legible.
rootCause: ID presence is used as a stand-in for join correctness, but the source join is name-keyed, so the ID is not the thing that was matched.
requiredRepair: Either rename the field to identityKeyKind (a categorical, not a score) or make 1.00 require ID presence AND position/source agreement, so it grades the join that actually happened.

title: POST /api/rankings/overrides rewrites the shared canonical rank snapshot on the stock frontend body, so every /rankings page load overwrites the baseline that the next scrape's rankChange arrows are measured against
claimUnderTest: _stamp_rank_changes docstring: 'write_snapshot=False is used on override / delta-payload builds so a user toggling sources on /settings doesn't clobber the canonical-board snapshot the scheduled scrape writes.'
observed: The guard is write_snapshot=not source_overrides. normalize_source_overrides skips reserved top-level knobs, so the stock frontend body {"tep_multiplier":1.15} yields source_overrides == {} — falsy — and the write happens. Verified live: md5 of data/snapshots/ranks_last.json changed from daa852fbd3babbed607bcb75a92a3388 to bf80856573367183427d889716823bc4 (size 14668 -> 14666) after one POST with that body. The ranks written are the TEP-1.15 board's ranks (W03-F001), which the canonical build never produces — so after any page load the next scrape's rankChange is default-vs-TEP contamination on top of any real day-over-day move. The delta path has the same hole: _for_delta exists but is not consulted at this call site.

reproduction.command: md5sum data/snapshots/ranks_last.json; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/rankings/overrides?view=delta' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tep_multiplier":1.15}' -o /dev/null; sleep 1; md5sum data/snapshots/ranks_last.json
reproduction.expected: identical md5 (a read endpoint must not write the canonical baseline)

userImpact: The up/down arrows in the '#' column, the Movers panel and signal-engine's 'rank rising N on the last scrape' are all measured against a baseline that any anonymous page load can overwrite with a different board's ranks. In a multi-user deployment the arrows are effectively non-deterministic.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed at runtime with a before/after md5 on the live stack; the prior audit reasoned it from the code path only. New detail: the ranks written are the divergent TEP board's, not the canonical board's.

whatWorks: The write is atomic-ish and non-fatal on failure; the canonical scrape path does write the right thing when it is the last writer.
requiredRepair: Gate on the request kind, not on the truthiness of source_overrides: pass write_snapshot=False from every /api/rankings/overrides path (and from delta builds) explicitly, and assert in a test that the file's mtime is unchanged by a POST.
rootCause: A guard written as 'no overrides means this is the canonical build' when 'no SOURCE overrides' and 'is the canonical build' are different predicates.
dependencies: Note for the audit itself: AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md lists /api/rankings/overrides among 'pure read' endpoints safe to POST. It is not — probing it mutates data/snapshots/ranks_last.json (gitignored runtime state, not a tracked file).

title: /api/movers and /api/data/rank-history return empty because data/rank_history.jsonl does not exist; the log is written only on a fresh-scrape promotion
claimUnderTest: /api/movers returns buy-low/sell-high signals from rank history; RankChangeGlyph renders a sparkline from row.rankHistory.
observed: GET /api/movers -> {"window":0,"windowRequested":14,"historyDepthDays":0,"threshold":15,"asOf":null,"risers":[],"fallers":[]} (106 bytes). GET /api/data/rank-history -> {"days":30,"history":{}} (24 bytes). The absent path is data/rank_history.jsonl. append_snapshot is called only under `if is_fresh_scrape` (server.py:1866), and the audit harness suppresses the scrape, so nothing seeds it in this container. Both endpoints degrade honestly — they report window 0 / historyDepthDays 0 rather than labelling a fabricated delta — and no row carries a rankHistory array, so the sparkline self-suppresses. Because the log is empty I could not test whether movers compares compatible snapshots at runtime; the code that would (date-anchored `newest_within` selection, per-entry spanDays, honestly-named currentSourceRanks) is present and looks correct, but is unexercised here.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/movers; echo; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data/rank-history; ls data/rank_history.jsonl
reproduction.actual: empty lists, window 0; ls: No such file or directory

userImpact: In this container: the Movers panel, the rank sparkline and the movement arrows are all blank. In production the exposure is the write path — one warning line on failure and a log that silently stops growing (the module's own docstring says so).

priorFinding.note: A23-F07 (movers anchors on the first snapshot present, so a '14d' label can be a 2-day delta) and A23-F19 (perSourceDelta does not exist) both describe code that has since been rewritten: server.py:3484-3517 now resolves the anchor by DATE against asOf-window, reports windowRequested vs the measured window, derives historyDepthDays from coverage() rather than the trimmed slice, and stamps per-entry spanDays; the field is named currentSourceRanks with a docstring that says it is not a delta. Not runtime-verifiable here — Blocked by data. PRIOR-A18-F21 (both history logs absent) is confirmed for rank_history.jsonl.

whatWorks: Both endpoints report their own emptiness in the payload (window 0, historyDepthDays 0, asOf null) instead of returning a fabricated window.
rootCause: Harness suppression of the startup scrape, plus a write path that only fires on fresh-scrape promotion.
requiredRepair: None in-product for the emptiness. Worth adding: a health check on coverage() so a silently-stalled log surfaces before a study needs it.

title: The per-source value-history log carries 2 of 21 sources because the startup backfill mines raw scraper exports, which never contain the 18 CSV-enriched sources
claimUnderTest: Module docstring: 'stores per-source values so the frontend can render "how each source has valued this player over time"', with a worked example showing ktc, fp_sf, dynasty_nerds_sf_tep and more.
observed: data/source_value_history.jsonl holds exactly one snapshot (2026-08-04, 840 players) and only two source keys: ktcSfTep (464 rows) and idpTradeCalc (814 rows). No `blended` key on any entry, and every key is suffixed ::unknown. Cause: the startup backfill (server.py:2643) mines data/dynasty_data_*.json — the RAW scraper export, whose player rows carry only ktc/ktcSfTep/idpTradeCalc; the other 18 registered sources are grafted on later by _enrich_from_source_csvs at contract-build time and so are structurally invisible to backfill_from_exports. GET /api/data/player-source-history?name=Josh%20Allen returns two series where the board blended 14 sources, and blended.value 9983 with derived:true (median of the two) beside a live board value of 9,988. The endpoint labels the reconstruction honestly, and the read path matches on name only so the ::unknown vs ::offense key change at the first real append will not split the series.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data/player-source-history?name=Josh%20Allen"; .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections; ls=open('data/source_value_history.jsonl').read().strip().split('\n'); o=json.loads(ls[0]); c=collections.Counter(); [c.update((v.get('sources') or {}).keys()) for v in o['players'].values()]; print(len(ls),'snapshots', dict(c))"
reproduction.expected: a series per contributing source (14 for Josh Allen)
reproduction.actual: 2 series (ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc); log-wide source coverage {ktcSfTep:464, idpTradeCalc:814}

userImpact: The PlayerPopup value-history chart claims to show how each source has valued a player and shows two of fourteen, with a reconstructed blend line 5 points off the live board value. A user reading source divergence off that chart is reading 14% of the evidence.

priorFinding.note: A18-F21 said both history logs are absent from the repository. source_value_history.jsonl is present here (startup backfill ran) — the defect is what it contains, which the prior audit did not measure. The backfill's blindness to CSV-enriched sources is new.

whatWorks: load_player_history stamps derived:true on reconstructed points rather than passing them off as recorded, applies the scope filter and the retired-key mask at read time, and matches by name so the key-shape change is survivable. The live append path (append_snapshot from the blended contract) would record all 14.
rootCause: backfill_from_exports treats the raw scraper export as if it were the blended contract; the two have different source vocabularies since source ingestion moved to post-scrape CSV enrichment.
requiredRepair: Backfill from exports/latest/ contract payloads (which carry sourceRankMeta.valueContribution for all sources) rather than data/dynasty_data_*.json, or run the export rows through build_api_data_contract before extraction. Also stamp a per-snapshot sourceKeys list so a two-source day is visibly a two-source day on the chart.

title: src/api/compact_view.py has no caller and its documented savings are off by 14x: view=compact is 7.36 MB, not the '~4MB to ~500KB' the docstring promises, and it still ships playersArray and the legacy players dict together
claimUnderTest: Docstring: 'Prunes fields that mobile / fast-first-paint views don't need so the payload drops from ~4MB to ~500KB uncompressed'; and it lists 6 pruned per-player fields.
observed: Live: GET /api/data = 11,953,535 bytes; GET /api/data?view=compact = 7,363,760 bytes — a 38% reduction, not 87%, and 14x the promised absolute size. The reason is that compact_contract prunes fields but keeps BOTH playersArray and the legacy players dict, which is the dominant duplication. _PRUNED_PLAYER_FIELDS actually contains 18 entries, not the 6 the docstring names (it additionally drops marketCorridorClamp, twoWayPlayerBoost, subgroupBlendValue, subgroupDelta, alphaShrinkage, softFallbackCount, hillValueSpread, marketDispersionCV, blendedSourceRank, madPenaltyApplied, anchorValue). Grepping frontend/ for 'view=compact' returns no non-test caller, so nothing takes this path today. It does correctly prune poolAudit/methodology/siteStats/sites and stamps meta.view='compact'.

reproduction.expected: ~500 KB and at least one frontend caller

userImpact: None today (no caller). The risk is a future mobile path being wired to a view that saves 38% instead of 87% and silently drops confidenceLabel — which frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx::confidenceExplain reads first — and blendedSourceRank, which is the CONSENSUS column.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed that the docstring names 6 pruned fields while the code prunes 18. REFUTED on the consumer: A12-F19 asserts 'Mobile and slow-network clients take this view (frontend/lib/device-profile.js:103-107)'; grep finds no non-test reference to view=compact anywhere in frontend/, so on this build the view has no caller at all. PRIOR-A01-F08 (compact prunes four fields the rankings UI reads) is therefore latent, not live.

whatWorks: compact_contract is non-destructive, prunes the four documented top-level blocks, slims sourceRankMeta to the three consumed keys, and stamps meta.view so a client can verify what it got.
rootCause: The docstring's size figures date from a build with a smaller contract and were never re-measured; the biggest win (dropping one of the two player collections) was never taken.
requiredRepair: Re-measure and correct the docstring, list all 18 pruned fields, drop the legacy players dict from the compact view, and either wire a caller or mark the module dormant.

title: The contract's methodology.confidenceBuckets block is now CORRECT — it publishes the percentile rule with the 30/80 pair explicitly nested as a non-live fallback; the prior 'publishes the wrong rule' finding does not reproduce
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A10-F01 / PRIOR-A09-F01: 'The contract publishes the wrong confidence-bucket rule; it misclassifies a third of the board.'
observed: The live block reads {"high":"2+ sources, sourceRankPercentileSpread <= 0.08", "medium":"... <= 0.2", "low":"single source, or sourceRankPercentileSpread > 0.2", "signal":"sourceRankPercentileSpread", "fallbackRule":{"appliesWhen":"caller supplied only sourceRankSpread (absolute ordinal); NOT the live /api/data path", "high":"... sourceRankSpread <= 30", ...}}. That is exactly the live rule, with the legacy pair correctly demoted and labelled. Recomputing every stamped bucket from the row's own sourceRankPercentileSpread + len(effectiveSourceRanks) gives 0 mismatches over 709 ranked non-pick rows. The prior audit's 33.3% figure is reproducible (I measure 34.0%, 241/709) but it is the rate at which the LEGACY rule would disagree with the live one — a difference between two rules, not a misclassification against the published one.

reproduction.actual: 0/709 stamped buckets disagree with the published rule; 241/709 (34.0%) would differ under the legacy 30/80 rule the block labels as non-live

userImpact: None — the panel is truthful. Recorded so the prior claim is closed rather than inherited.

priorFinding.note: Refuted on this build (HEAD e96c06ef): the methodology block now publishes the percentile rule as primary and the 30/80 pair under fallbackRule with an explicit 'NOT the live /api/data path' note. PRIOR-A09-F01 likewise refuted. The 33.3% number survives only as the legacy-vs-live rule difference (34.0% here), which is not a misclassification.

whatWorks: hasSourceDisagreement and anomalyFlags also recompute exactly — 0 mismatches over 740 ranked rows once the correct final denominator (len(tiered_rows)=740, not OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT=800) is used for the depth allowance. sourceRankPercentileSpread reproduces on 604/740 rows to 2e-4 with an approximate pool-size map; the 136 residuals are IDP rows where my pool-size approximation differs from the backend's per-scope count, not stamp errors.

title: frontend/lib/thresholds.js still exports the retired 30/80 ordinal cutoffs claiming to 'mirror the backend confidence bucket thresholds exactly', and edge-helpers uses one of them to suppress the Consensus-asset label on 49.6% of eligible high-confidence rows
claimUnderTest: thresholds.js:15 'These mirror the backend confidence bucket thresholds exactly. High: 2+ sources AND spread <= CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH'.
observed: CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH=30 / CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_MEDIUM=80 are the absolute-ordinal pair the backend demoted to a non-live fallback (see W03-F014). The header comment still says they mirror Python exactly. CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH has one live consumer: edge-helpers.js:87 gates the 'Consensus asset' SIGNAL label on row.sourceRankSpread <= 30 IN ADDITION to the backend's confidenceBucket === 'high'. On the live board, of 113 rows that are backend-high with >=2 sources and no disagreement flag, 56 (49.6%) are blocked from the label by that retired ordinal gate — e.g. 2027 Early 4th, sourceRankSpread 172 but percentile spread 0.0902. The row renders 'High' in the Confidence column and nothing in the Signal column, from the same underlying data.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,urllib.request; d=json.load(open('/tmp/f.json')); hi=[r for r in d['playersArray'] if r.get('canonicalConsensusRank') and r.get('confidenceBucket')=='high' and (r.get('sourceCount') or 0)>=2 and not r.get('hasSourceDisagreement')]; b=[r for r in hi if r.get('sourceRankSpread') is not None and r['sourceRankSpread']>30]; print(len(b),'/',len(hi))"
reproduction.expected: 0 rows blocked (the frontend gate should agree with the backend bucket)

userImpact: Half the genuinely high-agreement rows never get the 'Consensus asset' signal, so a user scanning the Signal column for safe assets misses them — and the two columns visibly contradict each other on those rows.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed that thresholds.js still mirrors the retired pair and still claims to mirror Python 'exactly'. New: the live consumer in edge-helpers.js and the 49.6% suppression rate it causes.

whatWorks: The backend bucket itself is correct and the frontend does read it — the ordinal gate is an extra AND term layered on top, not a replacement.
rootCause: A shared-constants module that was not updated when the backend migrated the rule, plus a belt-and-braces AND in edge-helpers that turned a stale constant into live behaviour.
requiredRepair: Delete the sourceRankSpread <= 30 term from edge-helpers.js (the backend bucket already encodes agreement), and either remove CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH/MEDIUM from thresholds.js or relabel them as the non-live fallback pair. Add a parity test in the spirit of tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py for threshold constants.
